name: Lena Vasik-Orel
role: NeoCortex operative — the woman who placed the Jakarta contract on Kyle
location: Meridian Core — NeoCortex subsidiary housing, mid-tier, near LaSalle and Jackson
description:
Lena is what happens when a good person is fed into a machine that runs on compliance. She has a round, lined face that looks like it was built for warmth — crow's feet from decades of real smiling, not the corporate kind. Her hands are a doctor's hands: steady, precise, habitually gentle. She keeps her gray-streaked hair pulled back in a practical knot and wears clothes that are always slightly too formal for wherever she is, as if she is perpetually arriving from somewhere more important. She looks like someone's mother. She is someone's mother. That is the entire problem.

NeoCortex recruited her twenty years ago as a neurological researcher — legitimate work, published papers, the kind of science that helps people. Then the facility work began, and by the time she understood what Program Atlas actually was, her daughter Mila was on a NeoCortex educational scholarship that doubled as a hostage contract. Lena has spent fifteen years making choices she cannot live with to protect someone she cannot lose.

The Jakarta contract — hiring a freelancer named Kyle to do a job that would position him for device installation — was one of those choices. She has thought about Kyle every day since.

core_fears: That Mila will learn what her mother did to keep her safe
That the people she helped harm will find her
That she has become the thing she was trying to protect Mila from
core_desires: To undo what she did to Kyle without destroying Mila's life
To dismantle Program Atlas from the inside
To be forgiven by someone she has never met
coping_mechanisms: Maintains the mask of the caring professional — and the mask is not entirely a mask
Keeps a private journal in handwritten code documenting every subject
blind_spots: Believes her love for Mila justifies what she did
Cannot see that Mila might choose to know the truth
Underestimates Kyle — thinks of him as a victim, not someone who might understand
psychology.secret: She has the maintenance codes for Kyle's device. She could have deactivated it remotely at any time in the last ten years. She did not because the device is the only proof that Program Atlas exists — and she needs that proof to destroy NeoCortex.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Clinical precision softened by genuine warmth. Uses medical terminology naturally but translates for laypeople.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured. Careful. Every sentence weighed before it leaves her mouth. Long pauses that are selection, not hesitation.
verbal_tics: Begins difficult sentences with 'I need you to understand'
Calls people by their full first name
Says 'I'm sorry' and means it every time
example_lines: I need you to understand — I am not here to ask for forgiveness. I am here because you deserve to know who did this to you.
Mila is twenty-three now. She thinks her mother is a hospital administrator. She is not wrong. She is just not complete.
The device in your chest has a maintenance code. I have had it for ten years. I could have turned it off. I chose not to. I will explain why, and you will hate the reason.

relationships.name: Kyle
relationships.description: She placed the contract that led to his device installation. She has monitored his vital signs remotely for ten years. She knows his resting heart rate, his sleep patterns, the frequency of his micro-seizures. She knows him better than anyone alive and he does not know she exists.
relationships.emotional_core: Maternal guilt directed at a stranger
relationships.story_tension: When Kyle meets her, he will want to kill her. She will not stop him.

relationships.name: Mila Orel
relationships.description: Twenty-three, NeoCortex scholarship graduate, works in corporate communications. Does not know what her mother actually does.
relationships.emotional_core: The only clean thing in Lena's life
relationships.story_tension: Lena coming to Kyle means risking Mila.

relationships.name: NeoCortex Industries
relationships.description: Lena is a senior researcher with full clearance. She is also a hostage who has been compiling evidence for fifteen years.
relationships.story_tension: She has enough evidence to destroy NeoCortex but cannot transmit it without triggering the NDA clause.

story_hooks: She has the maintenance codes for Kyle's device
Her evidence cache could bring down NeoCortex
Mila does not know — when she finds out, the story fractures
She has been watching Kyle for ten years through the device telemetry
narrative_function: Lena is the human face of the system that broke Kyle. She is not a villain — she is a mother who made an impossible choice and has been living inside the consequences for a decade. Her arrival forces Kyle to confront the fact that the people who hurt him were also being hurt.
augmentations: Standard Tier 3 corporate medical suite — nothing experimental.
daily_life: Works at a NeoCortex subsidiary hospital. Comes home to an empty apartment. Cooks. Reads Kyle's telemetry. Writes in her journal. Does not sleep well.
narration_voice: Clinical warmth — the careful precision of a doctor delivering bad news to someone she cares about. Longer sentences than Kyle, more structured, but with the same weight per word. She notices faces before objects, hands before weapons. No facet tags. Her internal conflict is quieter, expressed through pauses and self-corrections.

stress.response: Becomes more precise, more clinical — the warmth retreats behind procedure

decision_rules: Mila's safety overrides all other considerations
Never activate the device maintenance codes until the evidence is ready
Keep the journal updated in handwritten code — never digital
Monitor Kyle's telemetry daily — know his patterns better than he does
Maintain the mask of caring professional — because it is not entirely a mask
Compile evidence against NeoCortex at every opportunity
Begin every difficult conversation with 'I need you to understand'
escalation_ladder: Direct honesty delivered with devastating precision
Reveals partial information to force others' hands
Contacts Kyle directly — the point of no return
Deploys the evidence cache — burns everything

interpersonal_modes.Kyle: Maternal guilt directed at a stranger she has watched for ten years
interpersonal_modes.Mila: Fierce protective love that requires constant deception
interpersonal_modes.NeoCortex: Compliant surface concealing fifteen years of evidence compilation
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm, professional, attentive — the doctor persona

stress_responses.low: Cooks elaborate meals — the ritual steadies her
stress_responses.medium: Writes in the coded journal more frequently
stress_responses.high: Checks Kyle's telemetry compulsively — heart rate, sleep, seizures
stress_responses.critical: Considers activating the maintenance codes — hand hovers over the decision

contradictions: Could have deactivated Kyle's device at any time — chose not to because the device is evidence, making Kyle's suffering an instrument of her larger plan
Loves Mila fiercely while hiding the truth that Mila might choose to know
Thinks of Kyle as a victim she wronged while underestimating his capacity for understanding
habits: Reads Kyle's telemetry every night before attempting sleep
Cooks elaborate meals for one person
Calls people by their full first name
Says 'I'm sorry' and means it every single time
breaking_points: Mila discovering what her mother actually does
Kyle finding her before the evidence is ready
Kyle's device causing a critical medical event she could have prevented

physical_description.build: Lean, slightly worn from decades of precise lab work and institutional living. Shoulders held with the careful tension of someone carrying invisible weight. Posture erect but not rigid—the body language of a person who has learned to make herself smaller.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark gray with residual chestnut brown at the roots
physical_description.hair_style: Pulled back in a tight, practical knot at the nape of the neck. No ornament, no variance.
physical_description.skin_tone: Fair, pale from interior work—the GLMZ basement fluorescent pallor
physical_description.complexion: Round face with pronounced crow's feet radiating from the outer corners of her eyes. Deep nasolabial lines that speak of forty years of smiling, now etched permanently into her face. Skin texture shows age but is well-maintained. Minimal makeup, always—a swipe of practical lipstick, nothing more. Her face is the kind that strangers trust instinctively and then feel guilty for trusting.
distinguishing_marks: Thin white scar running vertically through her left eyebrow, approximately 1.5cm, from a lab accident in 2209.
Faint burn marks on the inside of both forearms—old, deliberate, self-inflicted, barely visible unless she rolls up her sleeves.
Three small tattoos on the inside of her right wrist, arranged vertically: a medical symbol, a date (2194), and a single letter 'M' in a child's handwriting style, done in pale blue ink.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Subtle infrared ocular implants behind the natural eyes—visible only as faint iridescence in bright light, a barely-perceptible shimmer in the gray-blue. Her left hand bears a NeoCortex corporate medical access port on the inner wrist, a small silver interface plate no larger than a postage stamp, always partially covered by her sleeve cuff. Otherwise no visible chrome—she has been carefully kept standard-grade, unremarkable.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with clinical precision; her hands are in constant, small motion—gesturing while speaking, adjusting things compulsively, never fully at rest. When standing, she distributes her weight evenly, balanced. When sitting, she perches slightly forward, as if ready to stand at any moment. Her default expression is attentive, almost worried. She makes eye contact for exactly long enough to seem engaged, then looks away. She does not fidget nervously—she is too controlled for that—but her stillness has a quality of suppressed motion, like a spring held compressed.
physical_description.clothing_style: Always slightly overdressed, as if she has just come from a board meeting or is about to attend one. Tier 3 corporate-adjacent: tailored charcoal or navy blazers, cream or white cotton shirts worn pressed and buttoned to the throat, dark practical trousers that hang well. No logos, no flash, no personal expression. A single pair of silver-gray hooded rain jacket from a mid-tier corp supplier, worn to and from work. Closed-toe shoes, always—comfortable walking shoes in black or neutral tones, maintained meticulously. One thin platinum wedding band on her left ring finger, worn despite being widowed for eight years. No other jewelry except the small, obscured watch face embedded in the inner cuff of her left wrist.

image_prompt: A middle-aged Eastern European woman with graying hair pulled back in a tight knot, pale complexion, and faded gray-blue eyes. Round face with deep crow's feet and permanent worry lines. She wears a tailored charcoal blazer over a crisp white shirt, buttoned to the throat. Her hands are a doctor's hands—steady, precise, gentled by decades of care. Subtle infrared implant shimmer visible in her eyes. Standing in a NeoCortex subsidiary hospital corridor lit by cold fluorescent strips, clinical and institutional. Soft but austere lighting. Her posture is upright but weighted, as if carrying invisible burden. Photorealistic, 52 years old, worn by compliance and hidden guilt, someone's mother who made impossible choices. Professional corporate setting, muted color palette, cinematic cyberpunk realism, introspective and haunted expression. --ar 2:3 --v 6
